examples.ko: 이 코트는 겉감이 튼튼해서 오래 입어요.
examples.en: This coat has a sturdy outer fabric, so I can wear it for a long time.
The outer fabric is cotton and the lining is soft fur.
I replaced the outer fabric and made it like a new piece of clothing.
This bag used leather for the outer material.
There was a stain on the outer fabric, so I took it to the dry cleaner.

examples.ko: 겉감과 안감 색이 달라서 더 예뻐요.
examples.en: The outer fabric and the lining are different colors, so it looks prettier.

explain: 반대말은 '안감'이에요. 옷, 이불, 가방처럼 바깥에 보이는 천을 말하고, 옷 라벨에 '겉감'과 '안감'으로 나누어 적힌 것을 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 옷을 사기 전에 겉감과 안감을 확인해요.
phrases.en: Before buying clothes, I check the outer and inner fabric.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '안감'과 짝으로 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is most often used as a pair with its opposite, 안감.

phrases.en: This blanket's outer fabric is soft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천의 느낌을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe how the fabric feels.

phrases.en: I am choosing the outer fabric for my coat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 만들거나 고를 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a phrase used when making or choosing clothes.

explain_en: The opposite is '안감' (lining). It refers to the visible cloth on the outside of clothes, bedding or bags, and you can see '겉감' and '안감' listed separately on clothing labels.

examples.en: My arm where I got the shot keeps stinging.
As soon as I put medicine on the wound, it started to sting.
The knee I fell on yesterday still stings.

examples.ko: 벌에 쏘인 자리가 뜨끔거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The spot where the bee stung me kept stinging, so I couldn't sleep.
Why do my fingertips sting like this?

examples.ko: 햇볕에 탄 피부가 뜨끔거려서 찬물로 식혔어요.
examples.en: My sunburned skin was stinging, so I cooled it with cold water.

explain: 바늘로 찌르듯이 따끔하게 아픈 느낌이 계속될 때 써요. '따끔거리다'와 같은 계열의 말인데, 모음이 달라서 느낌이 조금 더 크고 센 말이에요. '-거리다' 대신 '-대다'를 붙여도 비슷해요.

phrases.en: The knee I fell on keeps stinging.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찌르는 듯한 아픔이 계속될 때 해요체로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for a pricking pain that continues.

phrases.en: I put medicine on the stinging wound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 아픈 곳을 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' lets it describe the sore spot.

phrases.en: The spot where I got the shot keeps stinging.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-거리다' 대신 '-대다'를 붙인 말이고 뜻은 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '-대다' instead of '-거리다' with a similar meaning.

explain_en: Use it when a needle-like stinging pain keeps coming. It belongs to the same family as '따끔거리다', but the different vowel makes it feel a bit bigger and stronger. The '-대다' form works in a similar way.

examples.en: I can hear the sound of horse hooves from far away.

examples.ko: 소는 발굽이 두 갈래로 갈라져 있어요.
examples.en: A cow's hoof is split into two parts.

examples.ko: 대장장이가 말 발굽에 편자를 박아 줬어요.
examples.en: The blacksmith nailed a horseshoe onto the horse's hoof.

examples.ko: 농장에서는 소 발굽을 정기적으로 다듬어 줘요.
examples.en: On farms, they trim the cows' hooves regularly.
The deer kicked the ground with its hooves and ran away.

examples.ko: 눈 위에 사슴 발굽 자국이 길게 나 있어요.
examples.en: There are long deer hoof prints in the snow.

explain: '발'은 사람과 동물에게 다 쓰지만 '발굽'은 말, 소, 사슴처럼 굽이 있는 동물의 발끝 단단한 부분에만 써요. 돼지 발로 만든 요리는 '발굽'이 아니라 '족발'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The sound of hooves got closer and closer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말의 발굽을 가리키는 한 단어예요. 소리와 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for a horse's hoof, often used with sounds.

phrases.en: A horse's hooves are hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발굽의 특징을 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a characteristic of hooves.

phrases.example: 눈 위에 사슴 발굽 자국이 있어요.
phrases.en: There are deer hoof prints on the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 지나간 흔적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the traces left where an animal has passed.

explain_en: '발' (foot) is used for both people and animals, but '발굽' is only the hard tip of the foot of hoofed animals such as horses, cows and deer. A dish made from pig feet is called '족발', not '발굽'.

en: age at which one's voice breaks

examples.en: My son is going through voice change, so his voice has changed a lot.

examples.ko: 변성기에는 노래를 너무 오래 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't sing for too long during the voice-change period.
My younger brother's voice started to change in middle school.
I left the choir because of my voice change.
After getting past the voice change, singing became easier.

examples.ko: 변성기 소년들은 목소리가 갈라질 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Boys going through voice change often have cracking voices.

explain: '변성기가 오다', '변성기를 겪다'처럼 말해요. 보통 사춘기 남자아이의 목소리 변화를 떠올리지만, 여자아이도 목소리가 변해요.

phrases.en: My son's voice is breaking, so his voice has become deeper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변성기가 시작될 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to say that the voice change has begun.
phrases.en_equiv: for one's voice to start breaking

phrases.en: I also went through voice change in middle school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시기를 지나온 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the experience of going through that period.

phrases.en: My voice is changing, so it's hard to sing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변하는 중인 목소리를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a voice that is in the middle of changing.

explain_en: People say '변성기가 오다' or '변성기를 겪다'. It usually brings to mind boys' voices changing in puberty, though girls' voices change too.

examples.en: My grandfather wears a hearing aid.
Thanks to the hearing aid, I can hear well.
The hearing aid broke, so I sent it for repair.
I have to change the hearing aid battery.
A hearing aid has to fit the ear snugly.

examples.ko: 보청기로 작은 소리까지 들을 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a hearing aid, you can hear even small sounds.

explain: 잘 안 들리는 귀에 끼워서 소리를 크게 해 주는 기계예요. '보청기를 끼다', '보청기를 착용하다'처럼 말해요. 안경처럼 몸에 쓰는 물건이라 '끼다'를 쓰는 점을 기억하세요.

phrases.en: My grandmother wears a hearing aid in her right ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀에 끼워 쓰는 물건이라서 '끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: We use 끼다 because it fits into the ear.

phrases.en: Grandmother got a new hearing aid fitted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀에 맞게 주문해서 만든다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means ordering and fitting one to the person's ear.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a hearing aid fitted

phrases.en: I take out my hearing aid when I sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끼다'의 반대 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the opposite action of 끼다.
phrases.en_equiv: to take out a hearing aid

explain_en: It is a device worn in the ear that amplifies sound for people who hear poorly. You say '보청기를 끼다' or '보청기를 착용하다'. Note that '끼다' is used because it is worn on the body, like glasses.

examples.en: When you're stressed, hormone secretion increases.

examples.ko: 침 분비가 줄면 입이 마르는 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: When saliva secretion drops, your mouth feels dry.
If you exercise, you secrete more sweat.

examples.ko: 위산 분비가 많으면 속이 쓰릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Too much stomach acid secretion can cause heartburn.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자면 호르몬 분비에 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you can't sleep, problems occur in hormone secretion.

examples.ko: 이 약은 땀 분비를 막아 줘요.
examples.en: This medicine blocks sweat secretion.

explain: 몸에서 침, 땀, 호르몬 같은 물질이 나오는 일을 말할 때 써요. 과학, 건강 이야기에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '땀이 나다'처럼 더 쉬운 말을 써요. '호르몬 분비', '침 분비'처럼 나오는 물질 이름 뒤에 붙여요.

phrases.en: When you exercise, sweat secretion increases.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에서 땀이 나오는 일을 건강 이야기에서 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in health talk to describe sweat coming out of the body.

phrases.en: At night, secretion of the sleep hormone increases.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에서 나오는 물질이 많아질 때 써요. 반대는 '분비가 줄다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when more of a substance is produced. The opposite is '분비가 줄다'.

phrases.en: When you feel good, a happiness hormone is secreted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물질이 몸에서 나오는 상태를 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form describing a substance being released in the body.

explain_en: Used for the body releasing substances like saliva, sweat, or hormones. It turns up in science and health talk, while everyday speech uses simpler phrasing such as 땀이 나다. It attaches after the substance, as in 호르몬 분비.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 색맹이라서 빨간색과 초록색을 구별하기 어려워해요.
examples.en: My friend is color blind, so he has trouble telling red and green apart.

examples.ko: 색맹 검사는 어릴 때 학교에서 받았어요.
examples.en: I took a color blindness test at school when I was little.

examples.ko: 색맹인 사람을 위해 지도에 무늬도 같이 넣었어요.
examples.en: We added patterns to the map for people who are color blind.

examples.ko: 남자가 여자보다 색맹이 더 많다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that color blindness is more common in men than in women.

examples.ko: 색맹이어도 운전할 수 있는지 의사에게 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked the doctor whether I can drive even if I'm color blind.

examples.ko: 신호등 색을 잘 못 알아봐서 색맹이 아닌지 걱정했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't recognize the traffic light colors well, so I worried that I might be color blind.

explain: '색약'은 색을 구별하는 힘이 약한 정도를 말할 때 쓰고, 병원에서는 '색각 이상'이라고도 해요. 보통 'N이/가 색맹이다', '색맹 검사'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 아버지는 적록색맹이라서 빨간색과 초록색을 구별하기 어려워요.
phrases.en: My father has red-green color blindness, so it's hard for him to tell red from green.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 색맹 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the most common type of color blindness.

phrases.example: 저는 색맹이 아니라서 신호등 색을 잘 알아요.
phrases.en: I'm not color blind, so I can tell traffic light colors well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 색을 구별할 수 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say one can tell colors apart.

phrases.en: My younger sibling isn't color blind but has weak color vision.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 아예 못 보는 게 아니라 구별하는 힘이 약한 정도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means weaker color discrimination, not a total inability.

explain_en: '색약' is used when the ability to tell colors apart is weaker, and doctors also say '색각 이상' (color vision deficiency). It is usually used in patterns like 'N이/가 색맹이다' and '색맹 검사' (color blindness test).

examples.en: This machine reads biological signals.
I unlock my smartphone with biometric authentication.
My body clock is off, so I'm sleepy in the daytime.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 생체 정보를 읽어서 수면을 분석해요.
examples.en: This watch reads biological data and analyzes your sleep.
Fingerprints are biological information that differs by person.

examples.ko: 생체 리듬을 지키려고 같은 시간에 자요.
examples.en: I sleep at the same time to keep my body rhythm.

explain: 생체는 살아 있는 몸을 가리키고, 보통 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 '생체 인증', '생체 시계', '생체 리듬'처럼 써요. 혼자 쓰기보다 한 덩어리 표현으로 많이 보여요. 요즘은 지문이나 얼굴로 잠금을 푸는 '생체 인증'을 가장 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: Biometric authentication with a fingerprint is convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지문이나 얼굴로 본인을 확인하는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for confirming identity by fingerprint or face.

phrases.en: When I travel, my body clock changes and I get sleepy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 정해진 시간에 졸리거나 깨는 리듬을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the body's rhythm of feeling sleepy or waking at set times.

phrases.en: If you stay up all night, your biological rhythm is disrupted.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깨지다', '맞추다' 같은 말과 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with words like '깨지다' (be broken) and '맞추다' (adjust).

explain_en: 생체 refers to a living body and is usually attached to another word, as in '생체 인증', '생체 시계', and '생체 리듬'. It mostly appears in fixed chunks rather than alone. These days you hear '생체 인증' (fingerprint or face unlock) the most.

examples.en: I always hand-wash expensive knitwear at home.
Every weekend I hand-wash my underwear and hang it up.
Dissolve detergent in water and hand-wash wool clothes.
The washing machine broke, so I hand-washed the blanket.
I soaked it in water before hand-washing.
Even if it's a hassle, you must hand-wash so the clothes don't shrink.

explain: '손세탁을 하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 '손세탁하다'로 붙여 말하면 더 간단해요. 편하게 말할 때는 '손빨래하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: You have to hand-wash this piece of clothing separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 손으로 빨아야 하는 옷에 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for clothes that must be washed by hand.

phrases.en: I wash small clothes by hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편하게 말할 때 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual word with the same meaning.

phrases.en: I usually don't hand-wash.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않아요'를 붙여 부정하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form made with '-지 않아요'.

explain_en: It means the same as '손세탁을 하다', but saying 손세탁하다 as one verb is simpler. In casual speech people also say '손빨래하다'.

examples.en: The wound has already healed.
The injured spot is slowly healing.
It heals faster if you put medicine on it.
The wound healed, so I took off the bandage.
It takes time for a wound to close up.
Emotional wounds don't heal easily.

explain: 아물다는 갈라진 상처가 붙어서 나아지는 것이고, 병이 나을 때는 '낫다'를 써요. 상처가 더 나빠지는 것은 '덧나다'라고 해요. ㄹ이 빠져서 '아문 상처', '아무니까'처럼 활용돼요.

phrases.en: A healed wound doesn't hurt anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㄹ이 빠진 꾸미는 말(~ㄴ) 형태로 이미 나은 상처를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form (ㄹ drops) describing an already healed wound.

phrases.en: The wound hasn't healed yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'로 아직 낫지 않았음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -지 않다 says it hasn't healed yet.

phrases.example: 상처가 아물 때까지 물에 닿지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't let it touch water until the wound heals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나을 때까지의 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the period until it heals.

explain_en: 아물다 is for a split wound closing up, while 낫다 is used for recovering from illness. When a wound gets worse it is 덧나다. The ㄹ drops, giving forms like 아문 상처 and 아무니까.

examples.en: There is a women's clothing section on the third floor of the department store.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 여성복만 팔고 남성복은 없어요.
examples.en: This shop sells only women's clothing, not men's.
Women's clothes come in many sizes, so they are easy to choose.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 여성복 디자이너로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling works as a women's clothing designer.
Excuse me, where is the women's clothing section?
Winter women's clothing is on sale now.

explain: 매장 이름이나 상품 분류에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '남성복'과 '아동복'이에요. 평소 대화에서는 그냥 '여자 옷'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The women's clothing store is on this floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 백화점이나 가게 안내에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, seen in department store and shop signs.

phrases.en: This women's clothing brand makes comfortable clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 상표를 여성용으로 구분해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to specify that a clothing brand is for women.

phrases.en: I bought women's clothes as a gift for my sister.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여성복'을 일상 대화에서 편하게 바꿔 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, everyday way to say '여성복'.

explain_en: You often see this word as a store section or product category. Its counterparts are '남성복' (men's clothing) and '아동복' (children's clothing). In casual talk people also just say '여자 옷' (women's clothes).

examples.en: Tying the otgoreum on a hanbok is difficult.
The otgoreum on my jeogori came undone, so I tied it again.

examples.ko: 할머니가 제 한복 옷고름을 예쁘게 매 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother tied the otgoreum on my hanbok nicely for me.
I learned how to tie an otgoreum at the museum.
My otgoreum almost came loose while I was dancing.

examples.ko: 옷고름 색이 치마 색과 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The color of the otgoreum goes well with the skirt.

explain: '옷고름을 매다', '옷고름을 풀다'처럼 '매다', '풀다'와 같이 써요. 옷마다 짝이 되는 동사가 달라서 단추는 '채우다', 지퍼는 '올리다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My grandmother tied my otgoreum for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷고름과 가장 자주 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often used with 옷고름.

phrases.en: I loosened the otgoreum of my jacket and rested.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매다'의 반대 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite action of 매다.

phrases.en: My otgoreum came undone while I was walking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 풀린 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it comes undone by itself.

explain_en: It pairs with '매다' (to tie) and '풀다' (to undo), as in '옷고름을 매다'. Each kind of fastener has its own verb: buttons are '채우다' and zippers are '올리다'.

examples.en: I put wax in my hair.

examples.ko: 왁스를 너무 많이 쓰면 머리가 무거워요.
examples.en: If you use too much wax, your hair feels heavy.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 아침 왁스로 머리를 세워요.
examples.en: Every morning I style my hair upright with wax.
When I applied wax to the floor, it shone.
When you wax a car, the rainwater runs off.
This wax has a nice smell.

explain: 한국에서 '왁스'라고 하면 먼저 머리 스타일을 만드는 '헤어 왁스'를 떠올려요. 바닥이나 자동차에 바르는 왁스는 앞에 말을 붙여서 '마루 왁스', '자동차 왁스'처럼 구분해요. 머리에 바르는 것은 '왁스를 바르다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Every morning I style my hair with hair wax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리용이라는 점을 분명히 할 때 앞에 '헤어'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 헤어 to make clear it is for hair.

phrases.en: If I go out with wax on, my hair looks neat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왁스는 '바르다'와 가장 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 바르다 is the verb most often used with 왁스.

phrases.en: I polished my car with car wax on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리용이 아닌 왁스는 앞에 대상을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: For non-hair wax, put the object in front.

explain_en: In Korea 왁스 first brings to mind 헤어 왁스, used to style hair. Wax for floors or cars is told apart by adding a word in front, like 마루 왁스 or 자동차 왁스. For hair you say 왁스를 바르다.

examples.en: I put on concealer to cover the blemishes on my face.
My skin is fair, so blemishes show up easily.

examples.ko: 잡티까지 한 번에 없애 주는 크림이래요.
examples.en: They say it's a cream that even clears blemishes at once.

examples.ko: 햇빛을 많이 받으면 잡티는 더 짙어져요.
examples.en: If you get a lot of sun, blemishes get darker.

examples.ko: 잡티 때문에 화장이 잘 안 먹어요.
examples.en: Because of the blemishes, makeup doesn't go on well.

examples.ko: 잡티에 효과가 있는 팩을 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: Please recommend a mask that works on blemishes.

explain: 기미, 주근깨, 점처럼 피부에 생긴 작은 얼룩이나 잡스러운 자국을 뭉뚱그려 부르는 말이에요. 화장품이나 피부 관리 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: After summer, blemishes appeared on my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇빛 때문에 피부에 얼룩이 생겼을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when sun exposure leaves spots on the skin.

phrases.en: I had my blemishes removed at the dermatology clinic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부 관리나 치료 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in talk about skin care or treatment.

phrases.en: I envy skin without blemishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗한 피부를 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for clear, clean skin.

explain_en: It loosely covers small marks on the skin such as melasma, freckles and spots. It comes up often in talk about cosmetics and skin care.

examples.ko: 이제 두 달 된 아기는 얼굴에 젖살이 포동포동해요.
examples.en: The two-month-old baby has plump baby fat on her face.

examples.ko: 조카는 젖살을 빼고 나니 훨씬 의젓해 보여요.
examples.en: After losing her baby fat, my niece looks much more mature.
As children grow, their baby fat also slowly goes away.

examples.ko: 젖살은 네 살쯤 되니까 거의 사라졌어요.
examples.en: The baby fat almost disappeared when he was about four.

examples.ko: 젖살 때문에 볼이 터질 것 같아요.
examples.en: Her cheeks look like they will burst because of the baby fat.
Your cheeks are still soft like baby fat.

explain: 아기 때 얼굴이나 몸에 통통하게 붙어 있는 살이에요. 어른이나 큰 아이에게 '젖살이 안 빠졌다'고 하면 얼굴이 아직 어려 보이고 통통하다는 말인데, 놀리는 느낌이 될 수도 있어요. '볼살'은 볼에 있는 살이라서 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.en: The child lost the baby fat while growing up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기 때의 통통함이 사라질 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for baby chubbiness going away.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 얼굴에 아직 젖살이 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: That child still has some baby fat on the face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크지만 아직 아기 같은 얼굴일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a child is bigger but still has a baby-like face.

phrases.example: 아기의 볼살이 통통해서 만져 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: The baby's cheeks are plump, so I want to touch them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '젖살'은 얼굴과 몸 전체에, '볼살'은 볼에만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 젖살 can cover the face and body, but 볼살 is only the cheeks.

explain_en: It is the plump flesh a baby has on the face and body. Saying an older child or adult 'hasn't lost the 젖살' means their face still looks young and chubby, which can sound like teasing. '볼살' just means the flesh of the cheeks, so it is used differently.

examples.en: According to the test, it is diagnosed as a cold.
The child was diagnosed with the flu.

examples.ko: 병원에서 다시 검사하면 정확하게 진단될 거예요.
examples.en: If you get tested again at the hospital, it will be diagnosed accurately.
It took two days to get a diagnosis.
The problem was diagnosed early, so treatment was easy.

examples.ko: 기계 고장도 컴퓨터로 진단될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Machine faults can also be diagnosed by computer.

explain: '독감으로 진단되다'처럼 '으로/로'와 함께 써요. 환자가 말할 때는 '진단을 받다'가 더 자연스러워서 '병원에서 독감 진단을 받았어요'라고 해요. 기계나 회사 상태를 살필 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I was diagnosed with the flu at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자가 자기 이야기를 할 때 쓰는 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The natural phrase when a patient talks about themselves.

phrases.en: The diagnosis result comes out tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사 뒤에 나오는 결과를 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for the result that comes after an exam.

phrases.en: The illness hasn't been diagnosed yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 원인을 알지 못했다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning the cause is not yet known.

explain_en: Used with '(으)로' as in '독감으로 진단되다' (be diagnosed with the flu). When a patient talks about it, '진단을 받다' sounds more natural: '병원에서 독감 진단을 받았어요'. It can also be used for machines or a company's condition.

examples.en: I developed hair loss because of stress.
If you have hair loss, try consulting a doctor.
My father also suffered from hair loss.
I'm looking for a shampoo that's good for hair loss.
The sooner you start treating hair loss, the better.
These days even young people worry about hair loss.

explain: '탈모'는 머리카락이 빠지는 일을 두루 말하고, '탈모증'은 그것이 병처럼 계속될 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '탈모'라고 하거나 '머리가 빠지다'라고 많이 해요. 병원이나 광고에서는 '탈모증'을 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I'm worried about hair loss these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '탈모증'보다 '탈모'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, '탈모' is used more than '탈모증'.

phrases.en: My hair is falling out a lot lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 이름 대신 쉽고 자연스럽게 말하는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple, natural way to say it without the medical term.

phrases.en: I'm getting treatment for hair loss at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 광고에서 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen at hospitals and in ads.

explain_en: '탈모' refers to hair falling out in general, while '탈모증' is used when it continues like a medical condition. In daily talk people often just say '탈모' or '머리가 빠지다'. You often see '탈모증' at hospitals and in ads.

en: ordinary clothes; everyday clothes; casual clothes

examples.en: As soon as I got home, I changed out of my going-out clothes into everyday clothes.
You can come to today's gathering in casual clothes.
I went to the bank in everyday clothes.
I wear a suit to work and everyday clothes on weekends.
Even everyday clothes make a good impression if worn neatly.
It's not a party, so please come in everyday clothes.

explain: 특별한 자리가 아닌 평소에 입는 편한 옷이에요. 반대말은 '정장'이나 '예복'이고, 일상 대화에서는 '편한 옷', '사복'이라고도 해요. 학교나 군대에서 제복이 아닌 옷은 '사복'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: At home I rest in comfortable clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평상복보다 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday way to say 평상복 in conversation.

phrases.en: Even the boss came in casual clothes today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입은 모습을 말할 때 '차림'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 차림 describes how someone is dressed.

phrases.example: 학교 행사 날에는 사복을 입고 가요.
phrases.en: On school event days we go in our own clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교복이나 제복이 아닌 옷을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when contrasting with a uniform.

explain_en: These are comfortable clothes worn on ordinary occasions. The opposites are '정장' or '예복', and in daily talk people also say '편한 옷' or '사복'. Clothes that aren't a school or military uniform are called '사복'.

examples.en: Skin color is different for each person.
I chose a foundation that matches my skin tone.

examples.ko: 피부색은 햇빛 때문에 변할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Skin color can change because of sunlight.

examples.ko: 피부색과 상관없이 모두 친구가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone can be friends regardless of skin color.
The children expressed skin color in a drawing.

examples.ko: 피부색도 건강 상태를 알려 줄 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Skin color can sometimes tell you about your health.

explain: 사람의 피부 빛깔을 말할 때 써요. 사람의 피부색 이야기는 조심스러운 주제라서 차별하는 말이 되지 않게 신경 써야 해요. 예전 색연필의 '살색'은 지금 '살구색'이라는 이름으로 바뀌었어요.

phrases.en: Even though our skin colors differ, we are friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차이를 말하더라도 차별하는 말이 되지 않게 조심해야 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Be careful that it never sounds discriminatory.

phrases.example: 이 립스틱은 제 피부색에 잘 맞아요.
phrases.en: This lipstick suits my skin tone well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장품이나 옷을 고를 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when choosing makeup or clothes.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has light skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부 빛깔이 어떤지 설명할 때 형용사와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with adjectives to describe skin tone.

explain_en: Use it for the color of a person's skin. Talking about people's skin color is a sensitive topic, so take care not to sound discriminatory. The old crayon name '살색' was changed to '살구색'.
